question: In the exact MQSim state machine, can a finite ordinary overwrite trace leave unfinished GC operations after generation, host CQEs, host software queues and all simulated PCIe messages have drained?
purpose: source-derived reachability gate only; not P/PN information value or measured hardware
other_config: retain fixed source ssdconfig.xml including 0.05/0.005 GC ratios, RGA, NAND example latencies; no physical-device calibration claimed

workload.initial_fill: first 512 requests write sequential logical pages 0..511
workload.overwrites: remaining requests write page random.Random(913).randrange(512), common longest prefix reused

negative_control: 512 initial-fill-only endpoint; no manually injected GC/internal state
observer: passive counters/logs at existing flow generation end, host consume return, PCIe Deliver/after Consume, exact GC ongoing insertion/erase-removal, post-engine event and engine exit; no added simulated events or scheduling/control changes
host_boundary: finite generation done; generated=host-serviced=expected; software active and waiting zero; both simulated PCIe queues empty and no message callbacks in progress; recorded after whole event returns
gc_boundary: ongoing GC protected-block operations, includes queued/read/migration/erase phases; not automatically active NAND erase
limitations: no actual data bytes stored by MQSim host model
no next-task read or P/PN performance in this gate
simulated ns are sample config, not physical timing
acceptance: all expected commands complete and link messages drain, source-state GC trace has balanced start/end and no explicit engine stop; any GC>0 at accepted boundary is a model witness; all negative remains scoped to these four endpoints; zero unfinished GC at normal engine exit checked separately
failure_policy: preserve failure logs; fix instrumentation/build errors only, never change workload to obtain witness; if no clean completion report not established
protected: no production Linux/RTL/UAPI, no old experiments, no hardware; MIG1792023314 paused
